{"url": "https://api.crossref.org/works?query=epistemic+thresholds+for+independent+judgment+vs+consensus+adherence+in+multi-agent+reinforcement+learning&rows=4&select=DOI%2Ctitle%2Cabstract%2CURL%2Cpublished", "scope": "Crossref bibliographic metadata and abstracts where supplied; not full papers", "excerpt": "[{\"DOI\": \"10.1016/b978-1-55860-307-3.50049-6\", \"title\": [\"Multi-Agent Reinforcement Learning: Independent vs. Cooperative Agents\"], \"URL\": \"https://doi.org/10.1016/b978-1-55860-307-3.50049-6\", \"published\": {\"date-parts\": [[1993]]}}, {\"DOI\": \"10.1002/9781119699057.ch3\", \"title\": [\"Consensus Q‐Learning for Multi‐agent Cooperative Planning\"], \"URL\": \"https://doi.org/10.1002/9781119699057.ch3\", \"published\": {\"date-parts\": [[2020, 11, 6]]}}, {\"DOI\": \"10.2139/ssrn.6248881\", \"title\": [\"Stabilizing Independent Multi-Agent Reinforcement Learning via Curriculum-Based Iterative Self-Play\"], \"abstract\": \"<jats:p>Training stable and scalable policies in competitive multi-agent reinforcement learning (MARL) remains a fundamental challenge due to non-stationarity and severe exploration difficulties, particularly in high-dimensional continuous action spaces under decentralized independent learning. While centralized training architectures can alleviate these issues, they often incur poor scalability and increased coordination complexity. This paper introduces CRUISE (Curriculum-structured Reinforcement Learning via Iterative Self-Play), a training framework designed to stabilize independent deep reinforcement learning without employing centralized critics, joint policies, or explicit inter-agent communication. CRUISE structures the learning process through a progressive difficulty curriculum combined with iterative selfplay, enabling decentralized agents to break non-stationary cyclic behaviors (limit cycles) and acquire robust competitive strategies in otherwise unstable learning settings. We empirically evaluate the proposed framework on a high-dimensional, continuous-control competitive benchmark based on multidrone racing, using high-fidelity physics simulations to ensure realistic interaction dynamics. Experimental results show that standard independent reinforcement learning fails to converge as agent density increases, whereas CRUISE achieves stable learning, high success rates, and consistent scalability. Ablation studies further confirm that the curriculum structure is the critical factor enabling convergence, rather than policy architecture or reward design.
